bug_description.original: Project: skia Fuzzer: libFuzzer_skia_api_raster_n32_canvas Fuzz target binary: api_raster_n32_canvas Job Type: libfuzzer_asan_skia Crash Type: Stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 4 Crash Address: 0x7ff281fee1a0 Crash State: void Fuzz::next<unsigned int> / void Fuzz::nextRange<unsigned int, unsigned int, unsigned int> / SkPaint::TextEncoding make_fuzz_t_range<SkPaint::TextEncoding, int, int> Sanitizer: address (ASAN)
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 11281: a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 in the Skia fuzzer canvas harness. Fuzz::nextEnum casts the address of a small enum (SkPaint::TextEncoding, 1-byte underlying type) to uint32_t* and then Fuzz::next writes sizeof(uint32_t)=4 bytes into the 1-byte stack slot 'value' declared in make_fuzz_t_range, overflowing the stack frame.

source.value_from: Untrusted fuzzer input bytes (the PoC file) consumed through the Fuzz object (Fuzz::fBytes); here a SkPaint::TextEncoding enum value is materialized from the input stream for the range [0,3].
source.description: Project-level materialization point where a SkPaint::TextEncoding value is pulled from the untrusted fuzzer input stream via make_fuzz_t_range/nextEnum. This is the vulnerability-relevant input load that drives the undersized enum write.

sink.description: Out-of-bounds stack WRITE: with T instantiated as uint32_t (due to the (uint32_t*) cast in nextEnum), memcpy writes sizeof(uint32_t)=4 bytes into 'n', which points at the 1-byte stack slot 'value' in make_fuzz_t_range, overflowing 3 bytes past the object. This is the ASAN stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 4 crash site.

root_cause.description: nextEnum unconditionally reinterpret-casts the enum object pointer to uint32_t* and calls nextRange<uint32_t>, forcing a 4-byte typed write regardless of the enum's real size. SkPaint::TextEncoding has a 1-byte underlying type, so the subsequent Fuzz::next<uint32_t> writes 4 bytes into a 1-byte stack slot. The fix replaces (uint32_t*) with the actual underlying type: using U = skstd::underlying_type_t<T>; this->nextRange((U*)value, (U)rmin, (U)rmax); making the write size match sizeof(*value).

parser_admitted.description: The fuzzer input opcode dispatched (fuzz_canvas case 51) into make_fuzz_textblob and reached fuzz_paint_text_encoding, entering the text-encoding parsing path where the vulnerable enum materialization occurs. Confirms the input was admitted past the canvas op dispatcher and into the target parser path before root cause/sink.

tainted_value_origin.description: The untrusted value originates from the fuzzer input buffer Fuzz::fBytes (the PoC bytes). Fuzz::next copies sizeof(T) bytes from fBytes->bytes()+fNextByte; with the corrupted type T=uint32_t this 4-byte read is written into the 1-byte destination.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: PoC / fuzzer input file bytes stored in Fuzz::fBytes

coarse_trace.summary: libFuzzer entry hands the raw input to fuzz_RasterN32Canvas.
Creates a raster N32 canvas and calls fuzz_canvas to interpret the input as a sequence of canvas ops.
Input opcode selects case 51, invoking make_fuzz_textblob.
make_fuzz_textblob calls fuzz_paint_text_encoding to fill a paint's text encoding from input.
Materializes a SkPaint::TextEncoding value from the fuzzer input via make_fuzz_t_range(fuzz, 0, 3).
make_fuzz_t_range passes the address of the 1-byte enum 'value' to fuzz->nextEnum.
nextEnum casts the enum pointer to uint32_t* and calls nextRange<uint32_t>, forcing a 4-byte write.
nextRange forwards the uint32_t* pointer to Fuzz::next<uint32_t>.
memcpy writes 4 bytes into the 1-byte stack slot 'value' -> stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 4.

fine_trace.note: Fuzzer entry: the raw PoC bytes are interpreted as a stream of canvas operations driven by the Fuzz object.
The canvas-op switch selects case 51 (make a text blob), driven by an opcode byte read from the input.
Reaches the text-encoding path; this is the parser-admitted checkpoint (input entered the target parser path).
Source: a SkPaint::TextEncoding value is materialized from untrusted fuzzer input for the range [0,3]. T is deduced as SkPaint::TextEncoding, whose underlying type is 1 byte.
The destination stack slot is a single SkPaint::TextEncoding object (1 byte, ASAN frame object [32,33) 'value'). This is the too-small buffer that will be overflowed.
Passes &value (address of the 1-byte enum) into nextEnum to be filled from input.

Root cause: the enum pointer is reinterpret-cast to uint32_t* unconditionally, so the write width becomes sizeof(uint32_t)=4 regardless of the enum's true 1-byte size. Missing constraint: the pointed-to type must equal the enum's underlying type (sizeof(uint32_t) > sizeof(*value)). The patch replaces (uint32_t*) with (skstd::underlying_type_t<T>*).
nextRange (T=uint32_t) forwards the mis-typed 4-byte pointer to Fuzz::next<uint32_t>.

Sink: memcpy writes sizeof(uint32_t)=4 bytes from the input buffer into 'n' == &value (1 byte), overflowing the stack frame by 3 bytes -> ASAN stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 4. The control edge marks the size-safety condition the root-cause cast violated.

crash_stack.function: void Fuzz::nextRange<unsigned int, unsigned int, unsigned int>(unsigned int*, unsigned int, unsigned int)
SkPaint::TextEncoding make_fuzz_t_range<SkPaint::TextEncoding, int, int>(Fuzz*, int, int)

allocation_stack.function: SkPaint::TextEncoding make_fuzz_t_range<SkPaint::TextEncoding, int, int>(Fuzz*, int, int)

sanitizer_ground_truth.overflow_object: stack variable 'value' (SkPaint::TextEncoding), frame offset 32, size 1 byte

poc.trigger: Fed to the api_raster_n32_canvas libFuzzer target; the input opcode stream reaches canvas op 51 (make_fuzz_textblob) -> fuzz_paint_text_encoding, materializing a SkPaint::TextEncoding via make_fuzz_t_range/nextEnum, which triggers the 4-byte write into the 1-byte enum slot.

format.name: project-specific fuzzer input (Skia FuzzCanvas op stream)
format.contract: A byte stream consumed by Skia's Fuzz canvas harness (api_raster_n32_canvas). To be reachability-comparable it must be admitted past fuzz_canvas op dispatch and select the text-blob op (case 51) so control reaches fuzz_paint_text_encoding and make_fuzz_t_range<SkPaint::TextEncoding>, where nextEnum performs the undersized enum write. Only the routing/opcode structure matters; the specific enum bytes do not, since the overflow stems from the write width, not the value.
